The customer pin cannot itself carry an unlabeled constructed fact: logical.customer has no provenance attribute of its own, and chain/anchors/sources-v1.json anchors no ce.customer_* source, so there is no labeled constructed customer scenario for one to be mislabeled or omitted from in the first place.

sg.outcome.coverage_claim: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome enumerates exactly six outcome facts -- status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity -- that change as a trade moves through its life, describing that change entirely in terms of the trade's four named lifecycle statuses (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled). Each fact is handed off from raw.trade_cdc's own field for that fact (t_st_id, t_trade_price, t_chrg, t_comm, t_tax, t_qty respectively), typed mutable, with selector latest_change ordering candidate reports by the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order (batch_date, cdc_dsn) -- file production order, not a report carrying which file delivered it, which L1.hole.batch-identity leaves open. The anchored trade_code_meanings.cdc_flag states I as newly inserted and U as updating an existing record; both carry one of the clause's four named statuses, so latest_change's candidate set is I- and U-flagged reports, which inv.trade_outcome_updates_in_place restates directly. A cdc_flag D report is not one of these: 'deleted' is not a status the clause names, so latest_change does not select an outcome value from a D-flagged report; what a D-flagged report means for the trade's outcome -- whether it stands, is voided, or something else -- is L1.hole.deletions, not decided by this exclusion. All six facts the clause names are otherwise covered by a member of this group; the clause names no others.
sg.outcome.gap: L1.hole.deletions bounds what a D-flagged report means for a trade's outcome; L1.hole.batch-identity bounds latest_change's reliance on file production order rather than a report carrying which file delivered it.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_chrg->logical.tr.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's fees; raw.trade_cdc's t_chrg is the brokerage's own recorded charge value on each report, the fees fact the clause names.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_chrg->logical.tr.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_chrg on a trade_cdc row names the fees the brokerage charges on the trade, as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_comm->logical.tr.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's commission; raw.trade_cdc's t_comm is the brokerage's own recorded commission value on each report.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_comm->logical.tr.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_comm on a trade_cdc row names the commission charged on the trade, as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_qty->logical.tra.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's quantity; raw.trade_cdc's t_qty is the brokerage's own recorded quantity value on each report.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_qty->logical.tra.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_qty on a trade_cdc row names the trade's quantity, as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_st_id->logical.t.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report of a trade to update its status; raw.trade_cdc's t_st_id is the brokerage's own recorded lifecycle-status value on each report of the trade.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_st_id->logical.t.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_st_id on a trade_cdc row names the trade's lifecycle status as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_tax->logical.tra.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's tax; raw.trade_cdc's t_tax is the brokerage's own recorded tax value on each report.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_tax->logical.tra.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_tax on a trade_cdc row names the tax owed on the trade, as of that report.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_trade_price->log.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a later report to update the trade's executed price; raw.trade_cdc's t_trade_price is the brokerage's own recorded executed-price value on each report, distinct from t_bid_price, which records the price at which the trade was requested rather than executed and this job does not hand off.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_trade_price->log.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_trade_price on a trade_cdc row names the price at which the trade actually executed, as of that report.

inv.trade_outcome_updates_in_place.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade updates the outcome, describing that update entirely in terms of the trade's four named lifecycle statuses (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled); trade_code_meanings.cdc_flag anchors I as newly inserted and U as updating an existing record, both of which carry one of those statuses, so this invariant is the restatement of the update-in-place requirement over the six named outcome facts for I- and U-flagged reports specifically.
inv.trade_outcome_updates_in_place.parallel_assumption: Holds while every I- or U-flagged raw.trade_cdc row for a given t_id is a later report about that same trade rather than an unrelated new trade reusing the number.

logical.trade.commission.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its commission, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries commission directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.commission.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own commission fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no commission value yet, which the clause does not forbid.

logical.trade.executed_price.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its executed price, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries executed price directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.executed_price.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own executed-price fact once the trade has executed; a report of a trade that has not yet executed may carry no executed price yet, which the clause does not forbid.

logical.trade.fees.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its fees, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries fees directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.fees.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own fees fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no fees value yet, which the clause does not forbid.

logical.trade.quantity.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its quantity, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries quantity directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.quantity.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade report carries a determinable quantity, from the moment it is placed onward.

logical.trade.status.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its status, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries status directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.status.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade report carries a determinable lifecycle status (pending, submitted, completed, or cancelled).

logical.trade.tax.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires a trade's outcome, including its tax, to change as it moves through its life and requires a later report to update that fact; this attribute carries tax directly and is replaced by each later report.
logical.trade.tax.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade report supplies its own tax fact once determinable; a report of a trade not yet executed may carry no tax value yet, which the clause does not forbid.

type.trade_commission.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names commission as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from fees and tax.
type.trade_commission.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single commission value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

type.trade_executed_price.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names executed price as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from any bid or requested price.
type.trade_executed_price.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single executed-price value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

type.trade_fees.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names fees as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from commission and tax.
type.trade_fees.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single fees value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

type.trade_quantity.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names quantity as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact.
type.trade_quantity.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single quantity value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

type.trade_status.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names status as one of the outcome facts that changes as a trade moves through its life (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled); a dedicated value is indispensable to express that fact, replaced by a later report rather than kept beside it.
type.trade_status.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding names the trade's current lifecycle stage on every report.

type.trade_tax.necessity: L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome names tax as one of the outcome facts that changes through a trade's life; a dedicated value is indispensable to express that specific fact, distinct from fees and commission.
type.trade_tax.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tax value per trade report, replaced rather than accumulated.

sg.placement-moment.coverage_claim: L1.placement-moment fixes placement to the moment stated by the trade's earliest held report, in that report's own time. placed_at is handed off, under selector first_encounter_only, from whichever anchored source holds that earliest report: raw.trade_cdc's t_dts for a trade whose held reports are Trade change records ordered by trade_code_meanings.report_order's (batch_date, cdc_dsn), or, for a historical-load trade with anchored raw.trade_history rows, raw.trade_history's th_dts on its earliest such row instead, per report_order's statement that such a trade's earliest held report is its earliest TradeHistory row, not its Trade snapshot; inv.trade_placed_at_matches_earliest_report makes this rule itself checkable, not merely that placed_at is set once. Together the two handoffs carry exactly that moment, frozen, across both anchored report sources; owning_account_number still comes only from raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id regardless of which source supplies placed_at, since raw.trade_history carries no account field (sg.trade-shape). L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to be the pair of statements, account and customer, as they stood at that moment -- 'the account, and through it the customer, as they stood at the moment the trade was placed' -- not either one's current statement. L1.as-of defines each such answer as the upstream statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at; L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome's 'leaves the ownership as first recorded' is what fixes owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, and owning_customer_effective_from as frozen_from_first_encounter on this entity rather than per_statement, since that role belongs to the account and customer entities they are drawn from, not to how they behave once pinned here. owning_account_effective_from, handed off from logical.account.effective_from with selector as_of_event_time, completes the (account_number, effective_from) pair with owning_account_number (sg.trade-shape) that identifies the exact account statement. owning_customer_number is handed off directly from that same pinned account statement's own logical.account.owning_customer_number, so it can never name a customer inconsistent with it; owning_customer_effective_from, handed off from logical.customer.effective_from with selector as_of_event_time (also at or before placed_at), completes the (customer_number, effective_from) pair identifying the exact customer statement, satisfying the 'and through it the customer, as they stood' half of the clause in full -- not just which customer, but which of that customer's dated statements. inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen restates that all four reference attributes are set once, at first encounter, and never replaced. inv.trade_ownership_pin_present restates, as a single checkable fact, that a persisted trade never carries a null in any of these four attributes -- that the pin resolved, not merely that whatever it resolved to is frozen. first_seen_late, using the anchored trade_code_meanings.status_order and report_order, marks a trade whose first-encountered report -- across both anchored sources -- carries a status (th_st_id or t_st_id) other than PNDG as first seen late, which inv.trade_first_seen_late_matches_status_order restates directly. This coverage is conditional, not complete: L1.hole.change-effective-time bounds the account- and customer-statement pins against any upstream statement ownership-history has deferred (a CDC-sourced account or customer update); L1.hole.batch-identity bounds whether a report would also need to carry which file delivered it, which first_encounter_only and latest_change currently answer only via file production order (report_order) or, for raw.trade_history, th_dts ordering, not batch identity; L1.hole.closed-account-activity bounds a pin that lands on a closed-account statement whose status this job cannot verify against the trade's own later activity; L1.hole.deletions bounds what a cdc_flag D row means for a trade's first-encountered report and hence for placed_at and first_seen_late. Separately, L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account (recorded in holes) could change which account statement placed_at pins if its resolution re-versions accounts on a customer-only change.
sg.placement-moment.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time, L1.hole.batch-identity, L1.hole.closed-account-activity, L1.hole.deletions, and L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account each bound part of this group's coverage; see coverage_claim.

handoff.logical.account.effective_from->.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to name the account as it stood at the moment of placement; L1.as-of defines that answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment. This handoff selects, among the upstream ownership-history statements of this trade's owning_account_number, the one whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at, and freezes that effective_from as the second half of the (account_number, effective_from) reference identifying the specific account statement -- not the account's current statement.
handoff.logical.account.effective_from->.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a resolvable statement of this trade's owning account with an effective_from at or before placed_at.

handoff.logical.account.owning_customer_.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; the account statement already pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from carries, as its own owning_customer_number, exactly that customer. This handoff freezes that same value directly off the pinned statement rather than performing an independent as-of lookup, so the customer named can never be inconsistent with the account statement this trade's ownership pins.
handoff.logical.account.owning_customer_.parallel_assumption: Credible wherever the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from itself has a resolvable owning_customer_number.

handoff.logical.customer.effective_from-.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to name the customer as they stood at the moment of placement, not the customer's current statement -- 'and through it the customer, as they stood'; L1.as-of defines that answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment; L1.placement-moment fixes that moment to placed_at. This handoff selects, among ownership-history's logical.customer statements of the customer named by owning_customer_number, the one whose effective_from is the latest at or before placed_at, and freezes that effective_from as the second half of the (customer_number, effective_from) reference identifying the specific customer statement.
handoff.logical.customer.effective_from-.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.customer entity carries a resolvable statement of the customer named by owning_customer_number with an effective_from at or before placed_at.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_dts->logical.tra.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time. raw.trade_cdc's t_dts is that report's own recorded time; for a trade whose only held reports are Trade change records (every incrementally loaded trade, and any historical-load trade with no anchored TradeHistory rows), t_dts on the first-encountered such row is the earliest report the brokerage holds. For a historical-load trade with anchored raw.trade_history rows, the earliest held report is one of those instead (see the sibling handoff from raw.trade_history.th_dts), so this handoff and that one together, both under selector first_encounter_only, supply placed_at across the two anchored report sources; this handoff never takes a later report's t_dts.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_dts->logical.tra.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_dts on a trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report is the report's own stated time of that event, not a receipt or batch-load time, and while, for a historical-load trade, any earlier-held raw.trade_history rows are correctly preferred by the sibling handoff instead.

handoff.raw.trade_history.th_dts->logica.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time. For a historical-load trade, the brokerage's held reports include its raw.trade_history rows (per-status reports, one per lifecycle stage) as well as its raw.trade_cdc snapshot row; the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order states that such a trade's earliest held report is its earliest raw.trade_history row, not the snapshot. th_dts is that row's own recorded time, and this handoff takes it only from the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_history row (the one with the smallest th_dts), never a later one, and only when such rows exist for the trade.
handoff.raw.trade_history.th_dts->logica.parallel_assumption: Credible while th_dts on a trade's first raw.trade_history row is that report's own stated time of that lifecycle event, and while every historical-load trade's per-status reports the brokerage holds are exactly its anchored raw.trade_history rows (none held but unanchored). raw.trade_history's own anchored identifiers are (th_t_id, th_dts, th_st_id), not (th_t_id, th_dts) alone, so the anchors permit two rows of the same trade to share a th_dts with different th_st_id; this handoff assumes that does not happen among a trade's rows, since two rows tied for smallest th_dts would make which one is 'the earliest' -- and hence first_seen_late's status comparison -- ambiguous.

inv.trade_first_seen_late_matches_status.necessity: L1.placement-moment defines first seen late by reference to whether the earliest held report reflects the trade's true earliest lifecycle stage; this invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of first_seen_late's own derivation rule.
inv.trade_first_seen_late_matches_status.parallel_assumption: Holds while trade_code_meanings.status_order and report_order remain as anchored.

inv.trade_ownership_pin_present.necessity: owning_account_number, owning_account_effective_from, owning_customer_number, and owning_customer_effective_from are each declared nullable: false because L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade's ownership to be the account, and through it the customer, as they stood at placement -- a reference, not merely a value that may be present when convenient -- and L1.as-of together with L1.placement-moment defines that reference as the account's and customer's statements in effect at placed_at. The two as_of_event_time handoffs that complete this reference (logical.account.effective_from -> owning_account_effective_from and logical.customer.effective_from -> owning_customer_effective_from) are each credible only while a qualifying statement exists at or before placed_at. This invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of those four nullable: false declarations and that shared assumption: it decides nothing about what happens when a trade's pin does not resolve, only that a persisted trade carrying any of the four references as null is a violation an audit can name, rather than a silent gap invisible to compare.
inv.trade_ownership_pin_present.parallel_assumption: Holds while the four pin attributes' nullable: false declaration continues to state this job's intent that every persisted trade carries the reference in full; whether a trade whose pin cannot resolve should instead be persisted with the reference incomplete, dropped entirely, or handled some other way is not decided by this invariant and stays open under L1.hole.change-effective-time, which already bounds the statements this reference resolves against.

inv.trade_placed_at_matches_earliest_rep.necessity: L1.placement-moment defines placement as the moment stated by the earliest report the brokerage holds, and the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order states which row that is across the two anchored sources; inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen checks only that placed_at is set once and never replaced, not that the value it was set to is the correct earliest-report time. This invariant is the direct, checkable restatement of that correctness: without it, a placed_at wrongly fixed at a later report's time (for example, a historical-load trade's snapshot row instead of its earliest TradeHistory row) would still pass the 'set once' check.
inv.trade_placed_at_matches_earliest_rep.parallel_assumption: Holds while trade_code_meanings.report_order remains as anchored and every raw.trade_history row's th_dts and every raw.trade_cdc row's t_dts are each that row's own stated event time.

inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen.necessity: L1.placement-moment fixes placement to the earliest held report's own time, and L1.attribution-at-placement states directly that later changes do not move a trade that was already placed; this invariant is the restatement of that requirement over the placement-moment reference attributes.
inv.trade_placement_reference_frozen.parallel_assumption: Holds while a later report of a known trade, from either anchored source (raw.trade_cdc or raw.trade_history), never carries an earlier event time than the one already recorded as placed_at.

logical.trade.first_seen_late.necessity: Under the premise that every trade's lifecycle begins at PNDG (the first status in the anchored trade_code_meanings.status_order), L1.placement-moment requires a trade whose first-encountered report is not its true earliest lifecycle report to be marked first seen late, so the ownership placement fixes can be reviewed; a first-encountered report whose status is not PNDG -- the order's first status -- would then be exactly such a trade (SBMT for a trade never seen pending; CMPT or CNCL for a trade never seen submitted). L1.attribution-at-placement requires this marking, once made, to be fixed at first encounter and not reconsidered by a later report.
logical.trade.first_seen_late.parallel_assumption: Credible while every trade's lifecycle begins at PNDG, the first status in the anchored status_order, and while trade_code_meanings.status_order and terminal_status_codes exhaustively enumerate a trade's lifecycle statuses (PNDG, SBMT, CMPT, CNCL) with every trade report carrying one of them, and while report_order correctly identifies the first-encountered report across both anchored sources (the earliest raw.trade_history row when any exist for the trade, otherwise raw.trade_cdc's (batch_date, cdc_dsn) ordering). raw.trade_history's anchored identifiers (th_t_id, th_dts, th_st_id) permit two of a trade's rows to share a th_dts with different th_st_id, which would make the earliest row's status -- and so first_seen_late -- ambiguous; this derivation assumes that does not happen. PNDG is anchored as a limit order recorded but not yet submitted; a trade whose life legitimately begins at submitted (for example, a market order) would be mismarked first seen late under this premise, which is not resolved here.

logical.trade.owning_account_effective_f.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the account to be referenced as it stood at placement, not merely named; together with owning_account_number, this attribute completes the (account_number, effective_from) pair that identifies the specific account statement in effect at placed_at, per L1.as-of's 'latest statement that took effect at or before' the queried moment.
logical.trade.owning_account_effective_f.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a statement of this trade's owning account with an effective_from at or before placed_at; not yet resolvable where the correct statement is one of ownership-history's own deferred CDC-sourced account statements.

logical.trade.owning_customer_effective_.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership to reference the customer as they stood at placement, not merely which customer -- 'and through it the customer, as they stood at the moment the trade was placed'; together with owning_customer_number, this attribute completes the (customer_number, effective_from) pair that identifies the specific customer statement in effect at placed_at, per L1.as-of's 'latest statement that took effect at or before' the queried moment, and L1.placement-moment's fixing of that moment.
logical.trade.owning_customer_effective_.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.customer entity carries a statement of the customer named by owning_customer_number with an effective_from at or before placed_at; not yet resolvable where the correct statement is one of ownership-history's own deferred CDC-sourced customer statements.

logical.trade.owning_customer_number.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; this attribute carries that customer directly from the same account statement owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from already pin, so it can never name a customer inconsistent with that statement.
logical.trade.owning_customer_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account statement pinned by owning_account_number and owning_account_effective_from has a resolvable owning_customer_number.

logical.trade.placed_at.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of the trade the brokerage holds, in that report's own time; this attribute carries that moment, set once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report. The earliest held report may be a raw.trade_cdc row or, for a historical-load trade with anchored raw.trade_history rows, one of those instead; the two handoffs feeding this attribute together cover both anchored sources.
logical.trade.placed_at.parallel_assumption: Credible while the trade's first-encountered report, across both anchored sources (raw.trade_cdc and raw.trade_history), states its own event time.

type.trade_first_seen_late.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires a trade whose first-encountered report is not its true earliest lifecycle report to be marked first seen late, so the ownership placement fixes can be reviewed; a dedicated value carrying that marking is required to express it. L1.attribution-at-placement's 'do not move a trade that was already placed' requires this marking, once made at first encounter, never to be reconsidered by a later report -- frozen_from_first_encounter, not mutable.
type.trade_first_seen_late.parallel_assumption: Credible while the anchored trade_code_meanings.status_order and report_order let this job determine, at first encounter, whether the trade's lifecycle appears to have started before that report.

type.trade_owning_account_effective_from.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership to reference the account as it stood at placement, not merely which account; L1.as-of defines that answer as the account's statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before the queried moment; a dedicated value carrying that specific effective_from is required to complete the (account_number, effective_from) reference that identifies the exact account statement. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade 'leaves the ownership as first recorded'; on this entity (incremental_by_identity, not versioned), that reference is fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report, which is exactly the frozen_from_first_encounter role -- not per_statement, which describes a value's own kept-history nature on a versioned entity, a role that belongs to the account entity this value is drawn from, not to how it behaves once pinned here.
type.trade_owning_account_effective_from.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.account entity carries a statement of this trade's owning account whose effective_from is at or before placed_at.

type.trade_owning_customer_effective_fro.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's ownership reference to name the customer as they stood at placement, not merely which customer (already named by owning_customer_number) -- 'and through it the customer, as they stood at the moment the trade was placed'; L1.as-of defines that answer as the customer's statement whose effective_from is the latest at or before the queried moment; L1.placement-moment fixes that moment to placed_at. A dedicated value carrying that specific effective_from is required to complete the (customer_number, effective_from) reference that identifies the exact customer statement, fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report -- frozen_from_first_encounter, not per_statement, which describes the value's own kept-history nature on the customer entity it is drawn from, not how it behaves once pinned here.
type.trade_owning_customer_effective_fro.parallel_assumption: Credible while the upstream logical.customer entity carries a statement of this trade's owning customer whose effective_from is at or before placed_at.

type.trade_owning_customer_reference.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires that, through the account, the trade also belongs to the customer as that customer stood at the same moment; a dedicated value naming that customer is required to express that half of the clause. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome states directly that a later report of the same trade 'leaves the ownership as first recorded'; on this entity (incremental_by_identity, not versioned), that customer reference is fixed once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report, which is exactly the frozen_from_first_encounter role -- not per_statement, which describes the value's own kept-history nature on the account entity it is drawn from, not how it behaves once pinned here.
type.trade_owning_customer_reference.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account statement this trade's ownership pins has a resolvable owning customer.

type.trade_placed_at.necessity: L1.placement-moment requires the trade's placement to be the moment stated by the earliest report of it the brokerage holds, in that report's own recorded time -- across every anchored source of held reports, not only raw.trade_cdc; for a historical-load trade that is its earliest raw.trade_history row. L1.attribution-at-placement requires that a later change does not move a trade that was already placed; since this moment is what selects the account statement the trade references, it must be set once and never replaced, or a later report could shift which statement is selected and move the trade's ownership.
type.trade_placed_at.parallel_assumption: Credible while the earliest report of a trade the brokerage holds, across both anchored sources, states its own time, and that time is treated as the placement moment even when it is not the trade's true first lifecycle event (the first-seen-late case L1.placement-moment names).

sg.trade-identity.coverage_claim: Every raw.trade_cdc row carries t_id, the brokerage's own trade number, handed off unchanged into trade_number with the identity mutation role; because this value is identical across every CDC row reporting the same trade, no later report ever produces a 'different' trade, satisfying L1.identity's persistence requirement for the trade entity. inv.every_received_trade_persisted extends this group's claim from consistency to completeness: every trade_number none of whose received reports carries cdc_flag D appears as exactly one logical.trade row, not zero and not more than one.
sg.trade-identity.gap: L1.hole.deletions bounds this group's completeness claim: a trade_number with any cdc_flag D report is not claimed by inv.every_received_trade_persisted and stays that hole's case.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_id->logical.trad.necessity: L1.identity requires the trade's own number as its identity; raw.trade_cdc carries t_id as the brokerage's trade number on every row reporting that trade, including its first-encountered row and every later report.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_id->logical.trad.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_id values in this file are the brokerage's real trade numbers and not reused for different trades.

inv.every_received_trade_persisted.necessity: L1.identity requires a trade_number the brokerage already identifies to be the same persistent thing across every report of it, not a thing this job may simply fail to track. This invariant restates that persistence requirement as completeness rather than only as consistency (which inv.trade_owning_account_frozen and sg.trade-identity's own coverage already check): every trade_number carried by an anchored received report -- raw.trade_cdc (excluding cdc_flag D reports, per L1.hole.deletions) and raw.trade_history -- must appear as exactly one logical.trade row. A trade this job cannot pin (sg.placement-moment) is therefore a violation this invariant names, not a row the job is silently permitted to omit; together with inv.trade_ownership_pin_present, a trade whose pin does not resolve fires the same violation on every engine projection instead of being decided differently by whichever join shape a projection happens to use.
inv.every_received_trade_persisted.parallel_assumption: Holds while every raw.trade_cdc row with cdc_flag I or U, and every raw.trade_history row, reports a trade_number the business considers a real, receivable trade. L1.hole.deletions bounds what a cdc_flag D report means for a trade's persistence -- whether its trade_number must still appear as a row, must be removed, or something else -- so this invariant is quantified only over trade_numbers none of whose received reports carries cdc_flag D at all, leaving a trade_number with any D report entirely to that hole, not merely excluding the D-flagged report itself from an otherwise-qualifying trade. The anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order.note states that a historical-load trade's held reports are its TradeHistory rows together with the snapshot Trade row, so every th_t_id also appears as a Batch1 t_id (cdc_flag I, cdc_dsn 0); this invariant's raw.trade_history clause therefore rests on the entity's only identity handoff, raw.trade_cdc.t_id -> trade_number, which reaches every history-reported trade through that same snapshot row, not on a handoff this model does not define.

logical.trade.trade_number.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which trade a report is about and stays the same across every later report of that trade; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
logical.trade.trade_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's trade number is stable and unique per trade.

type.trade_number.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to a trade does not make it a different trade; a value invariant across every report of the same trade is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
type.trade_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's trade number is never reassigned to a different trade; if a trade number were reused for a different trade this role would misidentify reports, which should trigger review.

sg.trade-shape.coverage_claim: logical.trade's history kind, incremental_by_identity, is the direct consequence of L1.identity (a trade is a persistent identified thing; a later report about the same trade number is the same trade, not a new one), L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome (a later report updates outcome facts on this same row), and L1.attribution-at-placement (the trade's ownership, once established at placement, is never moved by a later report about the account or customer) -- together these entail one row per trade_number, updated in place, holding a frozen portion beside a mutable portion. The frozen portion's account-identity component is owning_account_number: raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id, taken only from the trade's first-encountered report and never replaced by a later one, which inv.trade_owning_account_frozen restates directly. This is the part of L1.attribution-at-placement that names which account a trade belongs to, fixed at first encounter; the remaining part -- which dated statement of that account, and through it which customer, stood as of the moment of placement -- is now resolved by L1.placement-moment and covered by sg.placement-moment instead, since that is the more specific claim. This group's own scope is limited to the entity's shape and the account-identity portion. That portion is nonetheless bounded: owning_account_number is taken from the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report, identified by the anchored trade_code_meanings.report_order (batch_date, cdc_dsn) -- file production order -- not from a report carrying which file delivered it, which L1.hole.batch-identity leaves open. It is also bounded by L1.hole.deletions: what a cdc_flag D row means is undecided, including whether the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report could itself be D-flagged and what that would mean for owning_account_number.
sg.trade-shape.gap: L1.hole.batch-identity bounds owning_account_number's reliance on report_order rather than a report carrying which file delivered it; L1.hole.deletions bounds what a D-flagged first-encountered report would mean for owning_account_number.

handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_ca_id->logical.t.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires the trade's own account be named and fixed at first encounter; raw.trade_cdc's t_ca_id is the brokerage's own recorded account number on the trade's first-encountered report, and this handoff takes that value only, never a later report's t_ca_id, per the clause's 'do not move a trade that was already placed.' raw.trade_history carries no account field, so this remains the only handoff for owning_account_number even for a historical-load trade whose placed_at is instead pinned from a raw.trade_history row.
handoff.raw.trade_cdc.t_ca_id->logical.t.parallel_assumption: Credible while t_ca_id on a trade's first-encountered report names the account the trade was placed under.

inv.trade_owning_account_frozen.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement states directly that later changes do not move a trade that was already placed; this invariant is the restatement of that requirement over the account a trade is recorded against.
inv.trade_owning_account_frozen.parallel_assumption: Holds while raw.trade_cdc never legitimately reassigns a trade to a different account after its first report; a contradiction would indicate a data error or an unaddressed business rule, not a value this attribute should adopt.

logical.trade.necessity: L1.identity requires a trade to be the same persistent identified thing across every report of it, not a new trade each time. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome requires that a later report of the same trade update its outcome (status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity) in place. L1.attribution-at-placement requires that a trade's ownership, once established at placement, is never moved by a later change to the account or customer, and that nothing the trade created is moved either. Together these entail exactly one row per identified trade, updated in place by later reports, holding a portion frozen at first encounter beside a portion that mutates -- the incremental_by_identity history kind, not versioned (which would keep every report as a separate dated statement) and not append_by_identity (which would treat every report as a new, unrelated event).
logical.trade.parallel_assumption: Credible while every raw.trade_cdc row, and every raw.trade_history row, for the same t_id/th_t_id is understood to be a later report about that same trade rather than a distinct trade reusing the number.

logical.trade.owning_account_number.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade to belong to the account it was placed under and forbids a later change from moving it; this attribute names that account, set once at first encounter and never replaced by a later report. raw.trade_history carries no account field (th_t_id, th_dts, th_st_id, batch_date only), so regardless of which anchored source supplies placed_at, this attribute is still, and only, sourced from the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report's t_ca_id.
logical.trade.owning_account_number.parallel_assumption: Credible while the account a trade is placed under is settled at the trade's first-encountered raw.trade_cdc report; whether a later report could legitimately correct it is not addressed by the clause and is not assumed here.

type.trade_owning_account_reference.necessity: L1.attribution-at-placement requires a trade to belong to the account it was placed under, and requires that a later change does not move a trade that was already placed; a value naming that account, set once and never replaced by a later report, is required to express that. L1.identity supplies the account's own persistent number as the value this reference carries. L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome's 'leaves the ownership as first recorded' is the clause that, alongside L1.attribution-at-placement, makes this value's role frozen_from_first_encounter rather than mutable.
type.trade_owning_account_reference.parallel_assumption: Credible while a trade's account assignment is settled at the trade's first-encountered report and never legitimately contradicted by a later report of the same trade.

clauses.L1.as-of: Any question about a customer or account can be asked as of a moment in time, and the answer is the statement in effect at that moment: the latest one that took effect at or before it.
clauses.L1.attribution-at-placement: A trade belongs to the account, and through it the customer, as they stood at the moment the trade was placed. Later changes to that account or customer do not move a trade that was already placed, and do not move anything that trade created.
clauses.L1.constructed-scenarios: Any scenario built to test these rules, rather than received from the brokerage's records, is labeled as constructed wherever it appears and is never mixed into the received records. A constructed scenario changes something the received records already know; it never introduces a customer, account, or trade the brokerage does not have. (Second sentence is an authorized clarification, assumed under `issue-8-statement-content-assumed`; review trigger: business confirmation.)
clauses.L1.current-version: The current statement about a customer or account is the one with no later statement. There is exactly one current statement per customer and per account.
clauses.L1.history: Every change to a customer or an account is kept, with the moment it took effect. Nothing about a customer or account is overwritten; a later statement sits beside the earlier one.
clauses.L1.holdings-follow-trade: A change in what an account holds is caused by a trade. The holding change belongs to whoever owned the trade that caused it, as that trade's ownership was recorded. Holdings are never re-attributed by looking the account up again later.
clauses.L1.identity: Customers, accounts, and trades are the things the brokerage already identifies: a customer number, an account number, a trade number. A change to a customer or an account does not make it a different customer or account; it makes a new dated statement about the same one.
clauses.L1.lifecycle-mutates-outcome: As a trade moves through its life (pending, submitted, completed, cancelled), its outcome changes: status, executed price, fees, commission, tax, quantity. Its ownership does not change. A later report of the same trade updates the outcome and leaves the ownership as first recorded.
clauses.L1.no-phantom-positions: Summing holding changes for any one statement of an account or customer can never go below zero. A negative result means a holding was opened under one statement and closed under another, which the clauses above forbid.
clauses.L1.omitted-facts-stand: A change that does not mention a standing fact leaves that fact as it last stood. A statement produced by such a change carries the fact at its last stated value. (Assumed under `issue-8-statement-content-assumed`; review trigger: the business confirms or amends.)
clauses.L1.owner-standing: An account's standing includes its owner's standing. When the brokerage says how an account stood at a moment, that includes how its customer stood at that same moment.
clauses.L1.placement-moment: A trade is placed at the moment of the earliest report of it the brokerage holds, as that report states its own time. A later report of a trade the brokerage has not seen before is treated as its placement and marked as first seen late, so the ownership it fixes can be reviewed. (Assumed under `issue-8-statement-content-assumed`; review trigger: the business confirms or amends.)
clauses.L1.statement-content: A dated statement carries the brokerage's standing facts at that moment. For a customer: whether the customer is active or inactive, and the customer's tier. For an account: whether the account is open or closed, its tax treatment, and which customer owns it. Names, addresses, contact details, and tax identifiers are not part of standing until a job needs them. (Assumed under `issue-8-statement-content-assumed`; review trigger: the business confirms or amends this enumeration.)

holes.L1.hole.batch-identity: Does a report need to know which incremental file first delivered a fact?
holes.L1.hole.change-effective-time: Incremental change files carry no time of their own. Does a change in such a file take effect at the file's batch date, or at some other moment?
holes.L1.hole.closed-account-activity: Trades appear on accounts the brokerage recorded as closed years earlier (account 428 closed in 2012, trades in 2017). Is that a data error, a reopening the records omit, or does a closed account still own trades?
holes.L1.hole.deletions: Incremental files can mark a record deleted. What does deleting a trade or account mean for history, ownership, and holdings?
holes.L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account: When a customer's standing changes, does the brokerage consider every account of that customer to have a new statement at that moment, or only the customer? The source data shows customer changes without matching account changes.
holes.L1.hole.securities-and-brokers: Securities, companies, and brokers are named in the records but not yet part of any job. When they are, the attribution rule must be restated for them.
holes.L1.hole.trade-timestamps: Which moment counts as "when it completed" when a later report of a trade arrives without its full history? (Placement is settled, provisionally, by `L1.placement-moment`.)

ownership-history.description: Know how any customer or account stood at any moment, and who owned what.
ownership-history.feedback: one current statement per customer and per account; statements of one thing do not overlap; any as-of question has exactly one answer with the standing facts of L1.statement-content; an account's as-of answer carries its customer's as-of answer

positions.description: Know what each account and customer holds, and how it got there.
positions.feedback: every holding change carries the ownership recorded on its causing trade; no statement of an account or customer sums below zero

trade-lifecycle.description: Know each trade's outcome and who owned it when it happened.
trade-lifecycle.feedback: a later report of a trade changes its outcome fields and leaves its recorded ownership byte-identical; ownership equals the account's as-of statement at placement, not the current one; placement is the earliest held report's own time
